baslik: Adhan and Iqamah (the call to begin prayer)
aciklama: A symbol of Islam announcing the time and start of obligatory prayers; the words and rulings of the adhan and the iqamah (the call to begin prayer).

kartlar.icerik:
In the dictionary, adhan means "to announce, to proclaim." It is the call made in specific words to announce the times of obligatory prayers.

The adhan is a symbol of Islam (a distinguishing sign of a religion or community) and is considered an emphasized Sunnah (a practice the Prophet ﷺ performed regularly and whose omission is discouraged). The person who calls the adhan is called a muezzin (the person who calls the adhan).

The Qur'an refers to the adhan in the words, "When you call to prayer..." (al-Ma'idah 5:58).
kartlar.vurgu: "When the time for prayer comes, let one of you call the adhan." (Bukhari, Adhan 17)

kartlar.baslik: The History of the Adhan — The Dream and the First Adhan
kartlar.icerik:
Salah was made obligatory during the Meccan period, but the adhan began after the migration to Medina. The Prophet ﷺ consulted the Companions about how the call should be made.

Proposals for a bell (Christian), a horn (Jewish), and a fire (Zoroastrian) were rejected. At this time, the Companion Abdullah bin Zayd learned the adhan in a dream; Umar had also had the same dream. The Prophet ﷺ approved it, saying, "It is a true dream."

The first adhan was called by Bilal al-Habashi, who had a powerful voice. (Abu Dawud, Salah 27)
kartlar.vurgu: First muezzin (the person who calls the adhan): Bilal al-Habashi | The one who had the dream: Abdullah bin Zayd

kartlar.baslik: The Words of the Adhan and Their Meanings
kartlar.icerik:
The words of the adhan, in order:
• Allahu Akbar (4 times) — "Allah is the greatest"
• Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah (2 times) — "I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah"
• Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah (2 times) — "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah"
• Hayya alas-salah (2 times) — "Come to prayer"
• Hayya alal-falah (2 times) — "Come to salvation"
• Allahu Akbar (2 times) — "Allah is the greatest"
• La ilaha illallah (1 time) — "There is no deity but Allah"

In the morning adhan, "as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm" (Prayer is better than sleep) is added twice after "Hayya alal-falah".
kartlar.vurgu: The adhan has 15 phrases, and the morning adhan has 17 phrases.

kartlar.baslik: Responding to the Adhan — What the Listener Does
kartlar.icerik:
A person who hears the adhan listens respectfully and, if possible, stops talking and other activities. They quietly repeat what the muezzin (the person who calls the adhan) says; this is called responding to the adhan (repeating the appropriate responses upon hearing it).

Exception: When "Hayya 'ala-s-salah" and "Hayya 'ala-l-falah" are called, one says "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (Power and strength come only from Allah).

When "as-Salatu khayrun mina-n-nawm" is heard in the morning adhan, one says "Sadaqta wa barirta" (You have spoken truly and well).

After the adhan ends, blessings are sent upon the Prophet ﷺ and the supplication after the adhan is recited.
kartlar.vurgu: Listening to the adhan is an act of good manners: if possible, remain silent, respond, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ and recite the supplication after the adhan. (Muslim, Salah 11)

kartlar.icerik:
After the adhan ends, the following supplication is recited:

"Allahumma Rabba hadhihid-da'watit-tammah was-salatil-qa'imah, ati Muhammadan al-wasilah wal-fadilah wab'athhu maqaman mahmudan alladhi wa'adtah."

Meaning: "O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the prayer about to be performed! Grant Muhammad the means and the virtue, and raise him to the Praised Station You have promised him."

The Prophet ﷺ promised his intercession on the Day of Judgment to the one who recites this supplication. (Bukhari, Adhan 8)
kartlar.vurgu: The one who recites the supplication after the adhan has been given the good news that they will receive the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ.

kartlar.icerik:
In Hanafi practice, the adhan is considered an emphasized Sunnah; some scholars have also regarded it as a communal obligation because of its role in the community. For this reason, omitting it is discouraged. The time for prayer must have begun before the adhan is called; an adhan called before the time begins is repeated once the time has begun, especially in Hanafi practice.

For the adhan in a mosque or congregation, the muezzin (the person who calls the adhan) is expected to be male, of sound mind, and to have a beautiful and powerful voice. It is recommended for him to have wudu (ablution); an adhan called without wudu is valid, although doing so is considered inappropriate.

Reciting slowly, with pauses between the phrases of the adhan, is called tarassul. Reciting the adhan distinctly and clearly is important so that the listener can respond (repeat the appropriate responses upon hearing it).

The adhan is recited in Arabic, and its prescribed order is observed.
kartlar.vurgu: The adhan is both part of the proper conduct of worship and a call to the community; its timing, order, and respectful recitation are important.

kartlar.baslik: What Is the Iqamah (the Call to Begin Prayer)?
kartlar.icerik:
The iqamah (iqamah) is the call announcing that prayer is beginning, made immediately before starting an obligatory prayer. In the dictionary, it means "to carry out, to set upright."

The same words as the adhan are recited; the only difference is that "Qad qamati-s-salah" (Prayer has begun) is added twice after "Hayya 'ala-l-falah".

It was taught in the same dream as the adhan. (Abu Dawud, Salah 28)
kartlar.vurgu: Iqamah = the words of the adhan + "Qad qamati-s-salah" (Prayer has begun)

kartlar.baslik: Differences Between the Adhan and the Iqamah
kartlar.icerik:
Adhan:
• Announces that the time for prayer has begun
• Is recited slowly and at length (with tarassul)
• May be called from a minaret or a high place
• Is a call for everyone

Iqamah (the call to begin prayer):
• Announces that prayer has begun
• Is recited more quickly
• Is recited within the congregation
• Is the call to proceed to prayer

There are detailed differences of opinion among the schools of law about women calling the adhan or iqamah among themselves and calling the adhan for a male congregation; in general practice, their calling the adhan for a male congregation has not been considered appropriate.
kartlar.vurgu: Adhan → the beginning of the prayer time, directed outward | Iqamah → the beginning of prayer, directed to the congregation

kartlar.baslik: Who Calls the Adhan and Who Calls the Iqamah?
kartlar.icerik:
Calling the adhan in the mosque is the duty of the muezzin (the person who calls the adhan). For a man praying alone, calling the adhan and iqamah (the call to begin prayer) is considered Sunnah or proper conduct.

The iqamah is called when beginning an obligatory prayer in congregation; it is a strongly emphasized Sunnah and organizes the transition to prayer.

A person who is in the mosque when the adhan is being called should not leave without performing that prayer unless there is a necessity; leaving is considered disliked.

A person who enters the mosque while the iqamah is being called should not remain standing but should sit down; they join the congregation when the imam begins the prayer.
kartlar.vurgu: Praying alone → Adhan + Iqamah are Sunnah or proper conduct | Congregation → Iqamah is a strongly emphasized Sunnah

kartlar.baslik: The Distinctive Feature of the Morning Adhan
kartlar.icerik:
The Fajr adhan differs from the calls to prayer at other times. After "Hayya 'ala-l-falah," "as-Salatu khayrun mina-n-nawm" (Prayer is better than sleep) is recited twice.

This phrase is a reminder specific to the Fajr prayer; it reminds people to rise from sleep and turn to prayer.

The schools of law differ in their practices concerning the timing of the Fajr adhan. In Hanafi practice, the adhan is recited after true dawn begins; if it was recited before the prayer time began, it must be repeated once the time begins. Some schools permit an early adhan for Fajr close to the start of its time.
kartlar.vurgu: "as-Salatu khayrun mina-n-nawm" — only in the Fajr adhan, twice

kartlar.baslik: The Wisdom and Importance of the Adhan
kartlar.icerik:
The adhan is not merely an announcement of the prayer time; it is also a declaration of iman repeated every day. In every adhan, Allah's greatness, the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and salah as the path to salvation are proclaimed.

At every moment, the adhan is being recited somewhere in the world, and Allah's name is raised without interruption, day and night.

The Prophet ﷺ praised those who love the sound of the adhan, listen to it, and respond to it by repeating the appropriate responses when they hear it.
kartlar.vurgu: The adhan is the daily renewed proclamation of Allah's oneness, prophethood, and salvation.

kartlar.baslik: Differences Between the Schools of Law
kartlar.icerik:
The essence of the adhan is the same across all schools of law; they differ in technical details:

• Ruling on the adhan: According to the Hanafis, it is an emphasized Sunnah; according to some scholars, it is a communal obligation (a responsibility fulfilled if one person in the community performs it).

• Number of takbirs: All four schools begin the adhan with 4 takbirs. The Maliki iqamah is shorter; the phrases of the adhan are not repeated in the iqamah, and most phrases are said once. The iqamah is the call to begin salah.

• Tarji' (repeating the testimonies of faith first quietly, then aloud): The Shafi'is perform tarji' with the testimonies of faith. The Hanafis and Malikis do not perform tarji'.

• Timing of the Fajr adhan: According to the Hanafis, an adhan recited before fajr as-sadiq (true dawn/the time when fasting begins) must be repeated. Some other schools permit an early adhan for Fajr close to the start of its time.

• A woman reciting the adhan: A woman reciting the adhan for a congregation of men has generally not been considered appropriate; the schools differ on whether women may recite the adhan or iqamah among themselves.
kartlar.vurgu: The essence of the adhan is the same; the differences are mostly in practice and technical details.
